domain_reasoning: Most time goes into opening the case, finding the order or account in the billing or order system and entering the refund, exchange or adjustment.
length_reasoning: A routine refund with a clear decision is entered in a few minutes; an exchange or multi-line bill adjustment needing record checks takes much longer.
review_reasoning: A supervisor or finance reader opens the case, checks the amount and account against the decision and the system entry.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount or account means money paid out incorrectly, which is a financial loss and awkward to claw back.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's billing system, remedy rules and posting codes, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the order or cancellation in the order or account system and handling any retention or confirmation screens.
length_reasoning: A simple order or cancellation takes a few minutes; one with many lines, payment details or a retention attempt takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the recorded contact, partly at speed, and checks the entered order or cancellation against what was said.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order or unwanted cancellation reaches the customer and causes rework or a complaint, but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's product catalogue, order system and cancellation policy, picked up over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing up a diagnosis and recommendation as a document or message, drawing on session notes.
length_reasoning: A short write-up of a clear issue takes a quarter hour; a complex diagnosis with evidence and options takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: A reviewer reads the write-up and checks the reasoning against session notes and logs; harder for long diagnoses.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis sent to a customer or developers causes wasted effort or wrong fixes, but is usually caught and reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs familiarity with the product, the customer's setup and the issue history, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading applications, interviewing and writing a recommendation, all in documents, conversation and messages.
length_reasoning: Screening a pool and holding several interviews takes a few hours for a thin pool and a couple of days of active work for a large one.
review_reasoning: HR and the hiring manager read the recommendation and check it against interview notes and criteria; longer when the field is large.
stakes_reasoning: A bad hire is costly and hard to reverse, and hiring errors carry legal exposure for discrimination.
context_reasoning: Judging fit needs knowledge of the team, projects and the employer's hiring conventions, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into operating the machine, installers, admin tools and the ticket system.
length_reasoning: A standard install from an image or package takes minutes; a repair with troubleshooting or a slow install takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: The lead checks the ticket notes and confirms the software runs, mostly a quick look.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty install is noticed quickly by the user and fixed, with little lasting harm.
context_reasoning: Standard tools and specifications are provided; a skilled outsider could do it, though local tooling takes a few weeks to learn.

domain_reasoning: Time goes into running and observing the software in the beta customer's environment and recording results.
length_reasoning: A short visit to a simple site takes half a day with notes; a complex site with load and integration checks takes more than a day.
review_reasoning: A test lead reads the findings and checks key observations against logs or screenshots; reproducing is excluded.
stakes_reasoning: Missed or misreported issues reach the product team and cause rework or a missed fix, but are reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the beta customer's environment, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is in monitoring dashboards, logs and profiling tools.
length_reasoning: Many anomalies are transient or known and closed in minutes to an hour; real regressions take hours to trace.
review_reasoning: A developer or lead reads the findings and checks them against graphs and logs; deeper issues take longer.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed anomaly usually recurs and is caught, but a missed real regression can become an outage.
context_reasoning: Telling noise from a real problem needs months of knowing this system's normal behaviour.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the remedy in the billing or order system.
length_reasoning: A simple refund or credit takes a couple of minutes; an exchange or adjustment needing lookups takes ten.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the call and checks the system entry and confirmation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount is usually noticed by the customer or at reconciliation and corrected, but larger adjustments can lose money.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's remedy rules, limits and billing screens, picked up over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is typing log entries describing transactions and installations through the day.
length_reasoning: Entries are made throughout the shift; a quiet day takes about 20 minutes of active writing, a busy one over an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor skims the day's log for completeness and checks a few entries against tickets.
stakes_reasoning: A missed or wrong entry is usually harmless, though it can matter at audit.
context_reasoning: Needs familiarity with local systems, ticket references and logging conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading configuration files, logs and code to find the cause.
length_reasoning: A clear failure with an obvious log error takes a few minutes; one needing code reading and reproduction takes hours.
review_reasoning: A developer reads the note and checks the cited log lines or code; harder to verify for subtle causes.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis wastes some developer time but is caught when they investigate.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of this codebase, its configuration and failure history, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is installing and configuring tools, often through config files, scripts and integration with build systems.
length_reasoning: A simple upgrade takes half an hour; a new tool with integration and configuration takes a day.
review_reasoning: A QA lead checks the tool runs and configuration is sensible by opening it and trying a few jobs.
stakes_reasoning: A broken tool blocks the team and is noticed soon, but is fixable.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's build setup, environments and conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into looking up requisition and invoice records in the billing system and preparing the return invoice.
length_reasoning: A simple full return takes a few minutes; partial returns across several lines with checks take longer.
review_reasoning: Billing opens the invoice and compares quantities and prices with the original records.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong return invoice misstates what the customer owes, which is a financial error that must be corrected with credit notes.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's invoicing system, pricing and returns rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running diagnostic commands and checking consoles on servers, printers and network devices, then recording results.
length_reasoning: A clean check takes about 15 minutes; one with several errors to log takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the round's record and spot-checks a few results against the systems.
stakes_reasoning: A missed error usually shows up later as a user complaint, but a missed real fault can become an outage.
context_reasoning: Knowing what normal looks like on these systems takes months.

domain_reasoning: The work is installing the build and running tests across many environments, which means operating applications and devices.
length_reasoning: A small matrix takes a couple of hours; a wide matrix with many failures takes days of active work.
review_reasoning: A QA lead reads the results and filed issues and spot-checks a few entries by reproducing them.
stakes_reasoning: Missed incompatibilities reach customers and cause rework or complaints, but can be patched.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's supported matrix and the team's test setup, built over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading requirements and writing a plan document.
length_reasoning: A plan for a small change takes an hour; a release plan with risks and scope takes a day.
review_reasoning: A test lead reads the plan and checks coverage against requirements; longer for large plans.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in a plan cause missed defects, found later and fixed, though a big miss can hit release.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the product, its risks and project history, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing a guide or procedure as a document.
length_reasoning: A short how-to takes an hour; a full guide with screenshots and testing takes a day.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the guide and may follow the steps to check them.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong steps mislead users and cause support requests, but are corrected once noticed.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the company's systems and users, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into completing the form or order in the account or contract system.
length_reasoning: A simple address change takes a few minutes; a contract or discontinuance with many fields takes longer.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the contact and checks the entered record and confirmation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong order reaches the customer and fulfilment and causes rework, but can be reversed; a wrong discontinuance is harder.
context_reasoning: Needs the employer's forms, products and rules, picked up over a few weeks.
